title: Data Preparation
text:
Step 2 Objective
This step prepares the career-market data used to evaluate opportunities for Data Analysts in financial services. The analysis is anchored to the project’s selected industry and career pathway:

Target career: Data Analyst / Data Analytics
NAICS: 523000
Industry: Securities, Commodity Contracts, and Other Financial Investments and Related Activities

The goal is to create a reproducible dataset that can be used to examine job availability, compensation, location, work arrangements, and employer characteristics.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Data Source
The project uses the MET Career Compass Employability API. The API provides job-posting information including job titles, employers, locations, salary fields, remote status, occupation classifications, NAICS classifications, skills, and job descriptions.
The API data used for this analysis was retrieved on October 5, 2026. The API reported a latest data refresh date of October 3, 2026 and identified the dataset as met-career-pathways-jobs.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Industry Filter
The first stage of the data preparation process restricted the job postings to:
NAICS 523000 — Securities, Commodity Contracts, and Other Financial Investments and Related Activities
The API returned 400 records matching this NAICS code before subsequent pagination requests timed out. All 400 retrieved records were verified to contain NAICS code 523000.
This industry restriction was retained throughout the analysis so that the project remained focused on financial-services employment opportunities rather than the overall labor market.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Career Filter
The target career pathway for Group 4 is Data Analyst / Data Analytics.
Several possible approaches were evaluated using the available occupation and job-title fields.

Occupation Classification Review
The MET data includes SOC and O*NET occupation classifications. SOC 15-2051 was initially considered because it is labeled Data Scientists.
However, the first 400 NAICS 523000 records demonstrated that this classification was too broad for the project’s specific Data Analyst pathway. For example, records classified under SOC 15-2051 included Android developers, iOS developers, mobile application developers, mobile engineers, and other roles that do not represent the target Data Analyst career.
Therefore, SOC 15-2051 was not used as a direct proxy for Data Analyst jobs.


Title-Based Career Filter
The final target-career filter uses explicit Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst terminology in the job title.
The inclusion logic identifies titles containing:

Data Analyst
Data & Insights Analyst

This approach was selected because it provides a more direct connection to the team’s stated career pathway than the broader occupation classifications observed in the data.
The resulting target-career dataset contains 2 postings:








Job
Employer
Location




Data & Insights Analyst (EMEA)
Greenparkcontent
London, United Kingdom


Advanced Data & Insights Analyst - Deposits Line of Business
U.S. Bank
Charlotte, North Carolina

title: Data Preparation
text:
Data Retrieval Limitation
The MET API successfully returned the first 400 records for NAICS 523000. Requests beginning at offset 400 consistently timed out, including requests for a single record.
Because the additional records could not be retrieved reliably, the project does not claim that the 400 records represent the complete NAICS 523000 labor market.
Instead, the retrieved records are treated as an accessible analytical sample from the MET Career Compass dataset.
This limitation is important when interpreting market-level results.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Cleaning Decisions

Duplicate Records
Job postings were checked using the MET job_id field.
No duplicate job IDs were identified among the 400 retrieved records.


NAICS
The naics_code field was converted to text and stripped of leading/trailing whitespace. Records were retained only when the resulting value equaled 523000.
All 400 retrieved records passed this verification.


Dates
Posting and expiration dates were converted to datetime values where available. Invalid or unavailable dates were treated as missing.


Salary
Annual and hourly salary fields were converted to numeric values. Missing salary values were retained as missing rather than being replaced with zero.
A missing salary does not imply that the position is unpaid; it indicates that a usable salary value was not available in the retrieved posting data.


Location
Location, city, state, and state-code fields were converted to consistent text values. Missing location fields were retained as missing.


Remote Status
Remote-status values were standardized to text categories such as remote, hybrid, onsite, or unknown. Missing or unavailable classifications were retained as unknown rather than inferred from the job description.


Skills
The API’s skills information was retained because skills will be used in later stages of the project to evaluate the capabilities associated with the target career pathway.


Occupation Fields
SOC, O*NET, and occupation-family fields were retained for comparison and validation. However, the analysis does not assume that a broad occupation classification is equivalent to the team’s specific Data Analyst career pathway.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Output Dataset
The cleaned target-career dataset is:
data/career_market_panel.csv
The dataset contains the two postings that directly match the project’s Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst title criteria.
A broader raw industry dataset is retained as:
data/raw_naics_523000.json
This raw dataset contains the 400 retrieved NAICS 523000 postings and provides the source data for industry-level exploration.
A variable-level data dictionary is available at:
data/data_dictionary.csv

title: Data Preparation
text:
Data Preparation Summary
The Step 2 preparation process can be summarized as:

Retrieve MET Career Compass job data.
Restrict records to NAICS 523000.
Verify the NAICS classification.
Review occupation classifications and job titles.
Reject SOC 15-2051 as a direct Data Analyst proxy because of substantial classification noise.
Apply a direct Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst title filter.
Remove duplicate job IDs.
Standardize dates, salary, location, remote-status, and occupation fields.
Export the cleaned target-career dataset.
Retain the broader NAICS dataset for market-level exploratory analysis.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Step 2 Limitations
The primary limitation is API pagination. The API returned 400 NAICS 523000 records, but requests beginning at offset 400 repeatedly timed out.
A second limitation is the small number of direct Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst postings within the accessible sample. Therefore, salary, remote-work, and other target-career statistics should be interpreted cautiously rather than generalized to the entire Data Analyst labor market.
The broader 400-record NAICS 523000 sample will provide additional industry context for the market-baseline analysis.

title: Data Preparation
text:
Conclusion
The data-preparation stage establishes a reproducible industry and career scope for the project. The analysis remains anchored to NAICS 523000 and the team’s Data Analyst/Data Analytics pathway.
The resulting datasets provide the foundation for the next stage: exploratory analysis of the financial-services market and evaluation of the skills, compensation, locations, and employment patterns relevant to aspiring Data Analysts. EOF

title: Market Baseline
text:
This page provides an exploratory baseline of the accessible job-posting sample for NAICS 523000 — Securities, Commodity Contracts, and Other Financial Investments and Related Activities.
The analysis uses the 400 NAICS 523000 postings successfully retrieved from the MET Career Compass API. The API returned 400 records before requests beginning at offset 400 consistently timed out.
The baseline therefore describes the accessible sample, not the complete financial-services labor market.

title: Market Baseline
text:
This page provides an exploratory baseline of the accessible job-posting sample for NAICS 523000 — Securities, Commodity Contracts, and Other Financial Investments and Related Activities.
The analysis uses the 400 NAICS 523000 postings successfully retrieved from the MET Career Compass API. The API returned 400 records before requests beginning at offset 400 consistently timed out.
The baseline therefore describes the accessible sample, not the complete financial-services labor market.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Job Volume by Title



Top job titles in the accessible NAICS 523000 sample


The job-title distribution is concentrated among several repeated postings. The most frequent titles include Android Software Engineer, Android Developer, iOS Developer, Mobile Application Developer, and Mobile Engineer.
This concentration demonstrates why job-title frequency should be interpreted carefully. Repeated postings can represent a small number of hiring campaigns rather than independent labor-market demand across many employers.
The target Data Analyst pathway is therefore evaluated separately using the direct Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst title filter described on the Data Preparation page.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Work Arrangement



Remote, hybrid, onsite, and unknown work arrangements


Remote work is the most common classified arrangement in the accessible sample.
The 400 records contain:

174 remote
56 hybrid
11 onsite
159 unknown

Approximately 40% of the postings have an unknown remote-status classification. Consequently, the observed remote-work pattern should be interpreted as a description of the available classifications rather than a complete estimate of remote-work availability.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Hiring Locations



Top hiring locations in the accessible NAICS 523000 sample


Location information is geographically diverse in the accessible sample.
The largest category is Unknown, with 116 postings. Among identified locations, China and Malaysia each account for 14 postings, followed by Hong Kong with 11 postings. Australia, Indonesia, Singapore, the United Kingdom, Taiwan, and Thailand each account for 10 postings.
The geographic distribution should therefore be interpreted cautiously because a substantial share of records does not contain a usable state or regional value.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Salary Information



Availability of salary information


Salary information is not consistently reported across the accessible postings.
Missing salary values were retained as missing rather than converted to zero. This distinction is important because an unavailable salary does not indicate that a position is unpaid.
Only postings containing usable annual salary minimum and maximum values were included in the salary distribution.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Annual Salary Distribution



Annual salary midpoint distribution


The salary distribution shows the range of annual salary midpoint values available in the retrieved postings.
Because salary reporting is incomplete, this visualization should be treated as descriptive rather than representative of all financial-services positions.
Salary comparisons for the specific Data Analyst pathway should also be interpreted cautiously because the direct target-career subset contains only two qualifying postings.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Experience Requirements
The retrieved records did not contain a dedicated experience-requirement field that could be reliably analyzed.
Rather than infer experience requirements from job descriptions, the project leaves this variable unreported in the baseline analysis.
This is an example of a data-quality limitation identified during Step 2 preparation.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Target Career Context
The project focuses specifically on Data Analyst / Data Analytics careers.
Within the 400 accessible NAICS 523000 records, two postings directly matched the project’s title-based Data Analyst filter:

Data & Insights Analyst (EMEA) — Greenparkcontent — London, United Kingdom
Advanced Data & Insights Analyst - Deposits Line of Business — U.S. Bank — Charlotte, North Carolina

These postings are retained as the target-career subset.
Other analyst titles were reviewed but excluded when their primary function appeared to be financial analysis, marketing, cybersecurity, compliance, strategy, engineering, or another specialized occupation.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Key Baseline Findings
The accessible NAICS 523000 sample indicates several important characteristics:

The market contains a wide variety of occupations beyond Data Analyst roles.
Remote work is common among postings with a classified work arrangement.
Geographic information is incomplete for a substantial portion of records.
Salary information is not consistently reported.
Repeated job postings can have a substantial effect on title-level counts.
The available data does not provide a reliable dedicated experience field.
Only two postings in the accessible sample directly matched the project’s Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst criteria.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Interpretation and Limitations
The market baseline should be viewed as an exploratory industry baseline, not a complete census of financial-services employment.
The primary limitation is API pagination. The MET Career Compass API successfully returned the first 400 NAICS 523000 records, but requests beginning at offset 400 repeatedly timed out, including requests for a single record.
A second limitation is the small number of direct Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst postings in the accessible sample.
These limitations are important because they prevent the project from making strong claims about the complete Data Analyst labor market, salary levels, or remote-work prevalence.
The results are therefore used to establish the available market context and identify data-quality issues that should be considered in later career evaluation and recommendations.

title: Market Baseline
text:
Step 2 Takeaway
The accessible NAICS 523000 sample provides a useful starting point for understanding financial-services job-market characteristics, but it also demonstrates the importance of careful career filtering and data-quality checks.
For this project, Data Analyst/Data & Insights Analyst titles are treated as the target career subset, while the broader NAICS 523000 records provide industry context.
